full_text_en:
Shaoguan Huifeng Huanan Chuangzhan Enterprise Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Provincial Environmental Engineering Equipment General Company and Guangdong Provincial Environmental Protection Engineering Research and Design Institute — contract dispute

Ruling Summary

Article 29 of the Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests an appropriate reduction, the people's court shall base its decision on the actual losses, taking into account comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the anticipated benefits, and shall make a ruling in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith. If the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused, it may generally be deemed as 'excessively high compared to the losses caused' as stipulated in Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law." When calculating the amount of actual losses, the calculation shall be based on the actual losses suffered by the non-breaching party as a result of the breaching party's failure to perform the contract that is the subject of the dispute and contains the liquidated damages clause, excluding losses other than those arising from the contract. For losses suffered by one party under other contracts, even if those contracts are connected to the contract in dispute, such losses cannot simply be used as the basis for determining the actual losses under the contract in dispute.

The provision in the aforementioned judicial interpretation that "the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused" shall be understood comprehensively and correctly. On the one hand, whether the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high shall be determined based on the specific circumstances of the case, taking the actual losses as the foundation, and considering comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the anticipated benefits, in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith. The "thirty percent" is not an inflexible fixed standard. On the other hand, the aforementioned provision addresses the standard for determining whether liquidated damages are excessively high, not the standard for the people's court to appropriately reduce liquidated damages. Therefore, in adjudicating cases, a court should neither mechanically treat any situation where "the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused" as automatically constituting "excessively high compared to the losses caused" under Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, nor, when legally "appropriately reducing the amount of liquidated damages," mechanically reduce the liquidated damages to one hundred thirty percent of the actual losses.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2011) Min Zai Shen Zi No. 84

Applicant for Retrial (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Respondent): Shaoguan Huifeng Huanan Chuangzhan Enterprise Co., Ltd. Domicile: Room C906, Yihe Plaza, Fengdu Middle Road, Zhenjiang District, Shaoguan City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Qiu Zhaoliang, General Manager of the company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Applicant for Retrial): Guangdong Provincial Environmental Engineering Equipment General Company. Domicile: 5th Floor, Provincial Agricultural Machinery Company Comprehensive Building, Wushan Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Hu Jibo, General Manager of the company.

Respondent (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance, Original Applicant for Retrial): Guangdong Provincial Environmental Protection Engineering Research and Design Institute. Domicile: 5th Floor, Provincial Agricultural Machinery Company Comprehensive Building, Wushan Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou City, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Hu Jibo, Director of the institute.

The applicant for retrial, Shaoguan Huifeng Huanan Chuangzhan Enterprise Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huifeng Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (2010) Yue Gao Fa Shen Jian Min Ti Zi No. 153 of the Guangdong High People's Court in a contract dispute with the respondents, Guangdong Provincial Environmental Engineering Equipment General Company (hereinafter referred to as Environmental Equipment Company) and Guangdong Provincial Environmental Protection Engineering Research and Design Institute (hereinafter referred to as Environmental Protection Design Institute). This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to review this case, and the review has now been concluded.

Huifeng Company applied for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The background for entering into the "Agreement" in question was that Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute failed to perform the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement" entered into with Huifeng Company. Although the "Agreement" in question stipulated a double liquidated damages clause, compared to the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement," the liquidated damages amounted to only three percent of the total project cost, which is a relatively low and reasonable penalty amount. Furthermore, the double liquidated damages clause bound both parties to the contract, not just one party. If Huifeng Company had breached the contract, it would also have borne corresponding liability for liquidated damages under the contract. There was no issue of inequality of status between the parties or manifest unfairness of the contract. 2. Considering the nature and purpose of the liquidated damages stipulated in the "Agreement" in question, the double liquidated damages were punitive in nature to ensure performance of the contract, did not violate legal provisions, and should not be adjusted. 3. Huifeng Company was the non-breaching party, while Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute breached the contract, causing substantial losses to Huifeng Company. Huifeng Company applied for retrial pursuant to Article 179, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China.

This Court is of the opinion: The issue is whether the people's court may adjust the amount of liquidated damages stipulated in the "Agreement" in question. Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the Contract Law) provides: "If the agreed liquidated damages are lower than the losses caused, a party may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to increase them; if the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high compared to the losses caused, a party may request the people's court or an arbitration institution to appropriately reduce them." In the absence of a clear standard under the Contract Law as to whether the amount of contractually agreed liquidated damages is excessively high, and in the absence of a corresponding judicial interpretation at the time of the first instance trial, the first instance court's judgment within the legal framework based on the case circumstances constituted the exercise of the judge's discretion. The Interpretation (II) of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as Judicial Interpretation II of the Contract Law) came into effect on May 13, 2009. Article 29 of this Interpretation provides: "Where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests an appropriate reduction, the people's court shall base its decision on the actual losses, taking into account comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the anticipated benefits, and shall make a ruling in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith. If the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused, it may generally be deemed as 'excessively high compared to the losses caused' as stipulated in Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law." According to the aforementioned provisions, liquidated damages have a dual nature of compensation and punishment. The parties to a contract may agree on liquidated damages that exceed the actual losses. However, given that liquidated damages exceeding thirty percent of the losses caused may generally be deemed excessively high, the nature of liquidated damages remains primarily compensatory, with the main function being to compensate for the losses of the non-breaching party, rather than to severely punish the breaching party. An excessively high agreed liquidated damages may conflict with the principle of fairness and, in some cases, may create a risk of moral hazard. Therefore, where a party claims that the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high and requests an appropriate reduction, the people's court shall adjust them in accordance with the law.

Regarding whether the amount of liquidated damages stipulated in the "Agreement" in question is excessively high. To determine whether the agreed amount of liquidated damages is excessively high, according to the Contract Law and Judicial Interpretation II of the Contract Law, the actual loss amount shall serve as the basis for confirmation. The term "actual losses" in the aforementioned provisions must be understood comprehensively and correctly. When calculating the amount of actual losses, the calculation shall be based on the actual losses suffered by the non-breaching party as a result of the breaching party's failure to perform the contract that is the subject of the dispute and contains the liquidated damages clause, excluding losses other than those arising from the contract. For losses suffered by one party under other contracts, even if those contracts are connected to the contract in dispute, such losses cannot simply be used as the basis for determining the actual losses under this contract. Huifeng Company argued that, although the "Agreement" in question stipulated a double liquidated damages clause, compared to the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement," the liquidated damages amounted to only three percent of the total project cost and were not high. According to the facts found in this case, although the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement" and the "Agreement" in question were related, they were ultimately two different contracts. When determining the actual losses caused to Huifeng Company by Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute's breach of the "Agreement" in question, it is inappropriate to calculate based on the total project cost involved in the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement." Furthermore, according to the facts found in this case, the "Agreement" in question stipulated that Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute would pay Huifeng Company more than RMB 1.56 million because the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement" was not actually performed. From the content of the "Agreement" in question, the aforementioned payment of more than RMB 1.56 million included both compensation by Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute for Huifeng Company's preliminary expenses and compensation to Huifeng Company for the termination of the contract. Therefore, Huifeng Company's argument that the liquidated damages were not high based on the total project cost of the "EPC General Contracting Cooperation Agreement" has no legal basis.

Regarding whether there was mechanical adjudication in this case. The provision in the aforementioned judicial interpretation that "the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused" must be understood comprehensively and correctly. On the one hand, whether the agreed liquidated damages are excessively high shall be determined based on the specific circumstances of the case, taking the actual losses as the foundation, and considering comprehensive factors such as the performance of the contract, the degree of fault of the parties, and the anticipated benefits, in accordance with the principles of fairness and good faith. The "thirty percent" is not an inflexible fixed standard. On the other hand, the aforementioned provision addresses the standard for determining whether liquidated damages are excessively high, not the standard for the people's court to appropriately reduce liquidated damages. Therefore, in adjudicating cases, a court should neither mechanically treat any situation where "the agreed liquidated damages exceed thirty percent of the losses caused" as automatically constituting "excessively high compared to the losses caused" under Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, nor, when legally "appropriately reducing the amount of liquidated damages," mechanically reduce the liquidated damages to one hundred thirty percent of the actual losses. The retrial judgment in this case upheld the first instance judgment. Considering the entire case, the first instance judgment's adjustment of the liquidated damages to thirty percent of the amount that Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute delayed in paying was not mechanical adjudication. On the one hand, when the first instance judgment became effective, Judicial Interpretation II of the Contract Law had not yet been promulgated. The first instance court's adjustment of the liquidated damages based on the specific circumstances of the case fell within the scope of its discretion. On the other hand, although Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute did delay payment, they fulfilled the payment obligation after a delay of just over one month. The amount of the delayed payment cannot be directly deemed as the actual loss amount of Huifeng Company. Considering the actual circumstance that Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute only delayed payment for a little over one month, the first instance judgment found that the agreed double liquidated damages were excessively high and calculated the liquidated damages at thirty percent of the delayed payment amount. This judgment actually constituted a comprehensive analysis of the specific circumstances of the case, the actual losses of Huifeng Company, and the degree of fault of Environmental Equipment Company and Environmental Protection Design Institute. There was no error in the application of law. Therefore, the result of the retrial judgment is not improper.

In summary, Huifeng Company's application for retrial does not meet the circumstances stipulated in Article 179, paragraph 1, item (6) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

The application for retrial by Shaoguan Huifeng Huanan Chuangzhan Enterprise Co., Ltd. is rejected.

Presiding Judge: Wang Huijun
Acting Judge: Wang Zhanfei
